title: Why Ethereum (ETH) Remains a Leading Cryptocurrency
subTitle:
Ethereum (ETH) is the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization and one of the most influential blockchain networks in the world. Unlike many digital assets that focus mainly on payments, Ethereum provides a platform for developers to build decentralized applications (dApps), smart contracts, and financial services without relying on traditional intermediaries.
One of Ethereum's greatest strengths is its large and active developer community. Thousands of projects are built on the Ethereum network, ranging from decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms to NFT marketplaces and blockchain-based games. This extensive ecosystem helps maintain Ethereum's position as a leader in the crypto industry.
Ethereum continues to evolve through network upgrades designed to improve scalability, security, and efficiency. These improvements aim to make transactions faster and reduce costs while supporting future growth.
For investors and blockchain enthusiasts, Ethereum represents more than just a cryptocurrency. It serves as the foundation for many innovations driving the adoption of Web3 technologies around the world.
As always, investors should conduct their own research and manage risk carefully before making investment decisions.
#Ethereum  #ETH  #Crypto  #Blockchain  #Binance

A few days ago, I was scrolling through Twitter and saw news that OpenAI's ChatGPT active user count hit a new high, and stories of corporate privacy breaches just keep coming. Everyone's feeding their privacy to these large models, and privacy agreements are just pieces of paper at the end of the day. Just in time, @OpenGradient  launched OpenGradient Chat, which claims to use a foundational architecture instead of verbal promises to achieve 'blind testing' of models like ChatGPT, even declaring itself a full-stack decentralized infrastructure.

Damn, as a seasoned trader with a research background, I had to dive in. I got up at 3 AM that night and went through OpenGradient's Python SDK, Model Hub, and this new Chat from top to bottom. Honestly, I was shocked; I had no idea until I looked into it, but after seeing it, all I can say is there's too much hype. #OPG 

To put theory into practice, I directly typed `pip install opengradient` in the terminal to run the model, but it kept throwing errors for ages. After sorting it out, I found that OpenGradient's daily hype about zero-knowledge proof (ZKML) verification was way off; running a basic ONNX regression model resulted in terrifying computation delays. #BTC 

If they really expect retail traders to run massive models with hundreds of billions of parameters using ZKML, the on-chain gas fees might just bankrupt them. Ah well, I had to settle for second best and switched to TEE mode in the SDK, which barely kept pace with Web2.

The most frustrating part is OpenGradient Chat, which claims to use privacy architectures like blind routing. But when I researched, I dug into the underlying data flow of the Model Hub and found that during inference, most requests are still interacting with their own centralized gateway. In other words, the underlying system is still a black box, and it's worlds apart from true decentralization. #ETH 

Honestly, right now, $OPG  is purely riding the hype of liquidity bonuses just hitting Binance and Upbit. If you take a clear-headed look, the computational costs of ZKML and the TEE mode's dependency on centralized hardware haven't been solved at all; regular developers can't afford it in the short term. It all looks exciting, but in practice, it’s just a cyber trap for retail traders—better to stay out of high positions.

OpenGradient focuses on a decentralized intelligence-exclusive network, claiming it can scale to support, run inference, and verify various AI models. Ah, this is very real, unlike those promotional videos that run smoother than centralized computing power. But the good news is, when I deliberately fed OpenGradient a contaminated logical weight, its distributed verification nodes really threw up an exception intercept. I'm impressed; this shows that OpenGradient's verification mechanism is indeed working and not just for show. $OPG

#opg  I've been meticulously reviewing the expense details of running machines on @OpenGradient  over the past two days, and it hit me—my previous understanding was way off. Initially, I thought it was just a hype-driven pump-and-dump chain, but after grasping the HACA mechanism and the underlying logic of SolidML, I realized they're operating an incredibly sophisticated order dispatch system. Here, the flow of tokens and the frequency of model calls are deeply intertwined. The amount of hash power credentials you lock directly determines your priority for order fulfillment and profit sharing. After running real data for three days, the release patterns matched the whitepaper perfectly; this is far from traditional mindless mining. $ETH #ETH 

After reconfiguring with this new mindset, the cost per simulation visibly dropped, effectively keeping the quick-profit hunters at bay. However, the cost was painfully steep; I took a silent loss during my second week in. The market was extremely volatile, and token prices were like a rollercoaster. I was eager to pull some $OPG  for a swing trade hedge, only to find the credential's freeze period was outrageously long. Liquidity was completely zeroed out; facing price surges and crashes left me anxious, stuck holding the bag while my assets shrank in value.

Besides being financially trapped, the onboarding process was incredibly torturous. Many seasoned coders complained that the official guide was incomprehensible, filled with obscure concepts like ZKML and TEE without any groundwork. The most critical question—'how to set up nodes to recoup costs the fastest'—had no answer, leading many to leave the group after just two days of trial and error. The high barrier to entry preserved the network's authenticity but physically deterred smaller teams looking for lightweight access.

@OpenGradient  relies on hardcore technology and mandatory lock-ups to prevent malfeasance, which is a solid direction. However, the ecosystem's prosperity can't solely depend on geeks holding the fort. If the obscure logic isn't neatly packaged to lower the learning curve, or if a flexible circulation mechanism isn't designed for the credentials to free up funds, even the most robust underlying framework will struggle to attract fresh capital.

OpenGradient宣传自己是开放智能专属网络，说白了就是一套去中心化基础设施，搞什么可规模化承载、运行推理并核验人工智能模型。@OpenGradient 宣传上最大的卖点，就是那个所谓的“可验证推理”，吹嘘能解决传统AI黑盒、不透明的痛点。体验之后，发现理想跟现实差了不是一星半点。#ETH 

我先是下载了OpenGradient的Python SDK，直接在本地跑。在部署一个轻量级分类模型时，我特意测试了OpenGradient引以为傲的x402支付协议里的不同结算模式。当我切换到INDIVIDUAL_FULL全链上核验模式时，卧槽，那个延迟简直让我崩溃，算力节点的上链确认慢得像蜗牛。虽然OpenGradient宣传有什么HACA架构，把计算和验证异步分开了，但真要在智能合约里做实时调用，这速度根本没法玩，妥妥的伪需求。
不过，当我体验他们的OpenGradient Chat时，倒是发现了一个细节。#OPG 

坏就坏在，把硬件TEE的活儿功劳全记在区块链账本上，ZKML概念炒得飞起，实际落地却因为算力成本太高，默认用的还是最便宜的BATCH_HASHED打包哈希。这本质上还是在卖服务器硬件信任，而不是纯粹的去中心化算法。#BTC 

清醒点讨论，$OPG 当前的行情完全是靠Binance上新和AI热点在硬撑。短期内由于50%的行业红利，代币OPG可能还有点波动机会。但长期来看，这种去中心化AI网络如果不能在推理成本上打败中心化巨头，最后大概率会沦为一个小众的隐私聊天工具。这就是典型的概念很丰满，实操很骨感。

title: Today Ethereum's core developers made one announcement that changes everything.
subTitle:
Today Ethereum's core developers made one announcement that changes everything.
Glamsterdam — the biggest Ethereum upgrade since The Merge — just entered its final development phase.
Public testnet is coming next week.
✦ On June 17, 2026 — today — Ethereum Foundation core developer Parithosh Jayanthi confirmed that Glamsterdam has entered its final development phase, with all planned EIPs now running on a developer network. He described it as "the final stage before codebase hardening and testnet launch" — and called Glamsterdam "probably the largest fork we have had since the Merge"
✦ If the ePBS testnet remains stable through this week, the first public Glamsterdam testnet will launch next week — followed by client releases, independent security audits, and full testnet validation before mainnet activation
✦ Glamsterdam combines two major upgrades in one — the consensus-layer Gloas upgrade and the execution-layer Amsterdam upgrade. The name itself reflects both components working together for the first time
✦ The three headline changes are EIP-7732, which brings block-building on-chain for the first time and reduces MEV manipulation by up to 70%; EIP-7928, which introduces parallel execution targeting 10,000 transactions per second; and EIP-7904, which reprices gas fees to reduce costs by approximately 78.6%
✦ For ordinary ETH holders — no action is required. Wallets, balances, and existing transactions are completely unaffected. Only validators and node operators need to install updated client software before mainnet activation
✦ Mainnet activation is now targeting end of August 2026 as the base case — after the original June 2026 target was pushed back when the Soldøgn interop devnet concluded May 2. The Sepolia and Hoodi public testnet activations will be the clearest leading indicator of when mainnet is imminent
Ethereum has been the most used smart contract blockchain on earth for years.
Glamsterdam addresses the two biggest criticisms it has ever faced — it is too slow and too expensive.
10,000 TPS. 78.6% cheaper fees. Final development phase confirmed today.
Public testnet next week.
Did you know Glamsterdam just entered its final development stage today — and that the public testnet could launch as early as next week?
#Ethereum #ETH #Glamsterdam #blockchain  #crypto

Back then, I thought it was just a power outsourcing scheme, making some fees by distributing tasks. But recently, after taking some time to think through its logic, I realized I had underestimated it. Simply running large models is not its endgame; what it's really planning is to establish a foundational 'ownership principle' for decentralized computing. #ETH $ETH 

Previously, everyone was used to focusing on processing speed and rental costs. But I later realized that packaging those scattered, unverified machine resources along with the auditing permissions into solid, on-chain standard certificates is its real ace in the hole. This way, GPUs are no longer just power-hungry metal blocks; they've transformed into liquid assets that can connect various on-chain financial and smart scenarios. It has effectively revitalized isolated nodes into a freely combinable value network.

A couple of days ago, I was going through the materials and even got a bit confused by the hardware isolation and cryptographic school verification mentioned in it. After revisiting it multiple times, I finally had an epiphany: this multi-faceted auditing system is the key highlight. In the future, whether it's a supergiant model or those compact vertical execution programs, as long as they go on-chain, the outcomes must be spot on. The industry doesn’t lack machines to do the work; what it lacks is a 'master key.' With this set of universally recognized rules, any level of configuration added can smoothly complete the loop of work, quality inspection, and payout, saving the hassle of setting up from scratch every time a new application arises.

Right now, the vast majority of competing products in the market are just battling over price cuts and speed. To be honest, once production capacity ramps up, this kind of profit will eventually be wiped out. In infrastructure, the ultimate battle will be about who holds the power to set the rules. This chain of operations turns the previously riddled privacy disguises into a thorny armor.

In actual experience, players spend $OPG  as fuel fees to freely connect with major mainstream models. Objectively speaking, creating such a distributed computing network, the slow response time is a hard issue that can't be avoided at this stage; how to stabilize the miners running nodes with a token economic model in the long term is also a hell-level challenge.

But nitpicking aside, compared to those air-drop coins, this approach of genuinely returning data ownership to the retail investors is a fundamental market need. $BTC #ETH  Analyst Qingshu
1. BTC looking rough? I see it as a short trap! You only see the drop from 67k to 64k, but ignore that the long-term weekly trend hasn’t broken. If it can bounce 8k from 59k, why can't it V-reverse from 64k straight back to 70k? That 'double dip at 60k' you see could be the last chance for the latecomers. Stop fixating on pocketing a measly 2% bounce; with the market opening up, wouldn't a direct spot buy here be more rewarding than playing with fire?
2. Is 64.3k strong support? If it breaks, you’ll be in shock. The market specializes in crushing 'self-assured defenses.' If 64.3k were that solid, it wouldn't have been pierced repeatedly today. You're suggesting to catch a 2% bounce above the support level; I see that as just handing the big players some fees. If you really want to bottom fish, why not place a buy below 62k for some bloody chips? Either don’t buy or go big. And about 'selling spot to buy back'—you just sold yesterday, and now you want in again? Aren't you worried about the fees?
3. ETH support at 1720-1730 looking decent? How many times has this level been tested? Another test means a break. You're telling everyone to catch a bounce first and then set a buy at 1640, but what if 1720 breaks directly? The order at 1640 might not even get filled while you're stuck halfway up. I say ETH should either charge up to 1730 right now or wait for below 1500; these middle levels are just mosquito legs. The same goes for SOL's 70 support—twice held doesn’t mean it will hold a third time. Looking for stability? Staying in cash is the safest play.
4. The notion of 'everyone escaping at the peak' is the most dangerous. If you sold BTC at 67.3k, ETH at 1840, and SOL at 66, that’s just luck, not skill. But what if you miss the next sell-off? You’re telling others to sell now, but when they see BTC at 64k, do they chase or not? Plus, you're flaunting 'past' exit trades—what about next time? If trading relied on showing past trades, everyone would have a lucky guess at some point.
5. 'Spot won’t get liquidated' is the biggest sedative I’ve heard. Spot doesn’t get liquidated, but you can get deeply stuck. If you buy from 60 to 75, that's a 30% gain, but what if SOL at 70 doesn’t hold and drops back to 55? Two weeks of profit could evaporate in a day. You’re constantly making trades; when you profit, it's 'we all win,' but when you lose, who takes the hit? If it's really that stable, just say 'hold and don’t move'—why all the daily fuss over buy and sell points?

In this position, either don't touch it at all, or mindlessly buy in batches; don’t calculate support levels for shorting. No matter how you calculate, in the end, it all comes back to you.

#ETH  In the crypto space, how can an average person level up? 
What books to read, what to study, to put it bluntly, it’s all useless. 
Sure, the knowledge in books is useful, and the experiences shared by successful traders are valuable. 
But you just can’t put it into practice; you have to walk the path yourself to know. 
The fastest way to boost yourself is through hands-on experience, get your hands dirty, don’t hesitate. Go ahead and lose some money, take a few hits, and you’ll quickly gain experience through failures and resets. If you’re making money without losing, you’re not gaining any experience. 
Focus on what you believe is good and just go for it, speculate on a target, and if you’re bullish, buy in early. 
The key is in being early; either believe it or don’t, but don’t chase highs—that’s the mantra to avoid FOMO. 
Don’t fear losing money; if you lose, you lose. It’s not a big deal. 
A friend said if it comes to it, I could just deliver takeout and start over or work in a factory; if you’re good-looking and willing to play the game, finding a sugar mama isn’t off the table either. 
Once you step into crypto, you get hooked and obsessed, almost wanting to sell everything you own to dive deeper into it. 
I used to be in the crypto game, checking charts daily, watching the market fluctuate; every shift felt like a Ferrari. 
That feeling kept my brain on edge all the time. 
After a while, my threshold for excitement increased, and I lost interest in everything else. 
A friend said I lost interest in women, games, and all forms of fun. 
Only seeing rising numbers brings a hint of a smile. 
Eating king crab or street fried rice feels the same to me. 
Even a stunning actress or someone like Feng Jie looks the same to me. 
It boils down to three words: no interest. 
That’s the price of playing in the crypto space. 
If you haven’t entered this field, try not to. 
Now that I’m in, just like many others, I can’t get out. 
Fun and leisure are things others yearn for, but for me, it’s just a string of numbers. 
Every market fluctuation seems to make my heart race; it makes me feel alive. 
At this point, crypto is my career. 
Boring, tedious, lonely; that’s my summary of the crypto world. 
Going to any temple for enlightenment, or listening to spiritual lessons is no match for leveling up in crypto. 
In the end, I’m only obsessed with numbers, forgetting all the love and hate of the world. 
The market is always there, but the rhythm waits for no one.

title: La Russie ouvre la porte à l'USDC : Un tournant pour le marché crypto local
subTitle:
Le paysage crypto russe est en pleine mutation. Selon les récentes déclarations d'Ivan Chebeskov, ministre adjoint des Finances, la Russie s'apprête à muscler sa liste d'actifs autorisés pour le trading en y intégrant officiellement l'USDC.
Les points clés de l'annonce :
L'USDC rejoint le cercle fermé : Après le Bitcoin (BTC), l'Ethereum (ETH) et l'USDT, le stablecoin de Circle va officiellement intégrer la liste des cryptos approuvées pour les échanges en Russie.Cap sur les stablecoins « amis » : Au-delà des géants du marché, le ministère envisage d'autoriser des stablecoins plus modestes émis depuis des juridictions partenaires, incluant des solutions adossées au rouble ou au dirham des Émirats arabes unis (AED).Un désaccord avec la Banque Centrale : Malgré une position initiale prudente de la Banque centrale russe — qui souhaitait limiter le nombre de tokens — le ministère des Finances maintient son cap vers une ouverture encadrée.
Ce qu'il faut retenir pour les investisseurs :
Le gouvernement russe finalise un cadre réglementaire strict, dont l'adoption est prévue avant le 1er juillet. L'objectif est clair : légaliser l'accès aux cryptomonnaies pour le grand public sous certaines conditions :
Critères de sélection : Pour être éligible au trading, un actif devra justifier d'une capitalisation boursière moyenne supérieure à 5 billions de roubles sur les deux dernières années.Protection des particuliers : Les investisseurs non professionnels bénéficieront d'un accès légal au marché, assorti d'un plafond d'investissement annuel fixé à 300 000 roubles.
Cette manœuvre marque une étape décisive pour la démocratisation de l'accès aux actifs numériques en Russie, tout en essayant de maintenir un contrôle sur les flux financiers.
#BTC  #ETH  #USDT  #USDC

quoteContent.body: 2026会再次走向1973的石油危机吗？btc会大崩盘吗？
quoteContent.title: 2026会再次走向1973的石油危机吗？btc会大崩盘吗？
quoteContent.bodyTextOnly:
今天我来聊聊一个被很多人忽略的历史老梗——1973-1974年的石油禁运，历史不会简单的重复，但是会极其相似。1973年发生的事情和2026年正在发生的事情极其相识。

1973年10月，阿拉伯国家一纸禁运，全球石油供应卡脖子。油价直接翻了好几倍，美股下跌大概20%。当时市场一片哀嚎：“完了，能源危机要命！
2026年川普和伊朗的战争，油价涨到了120美金以上，市场也认为能源危机到来了。
 1974年3月禁运正式解除，大家松口气：“危机结束了，石油要回来了，牛市要来了！”  然后呢？真正的屠杀才刚开始。
从解除那一刻起，美股像失重一样往下坠，后续几周暴跌近40%，全年熊市总跌幅接近50%。大萧条以来最狠的一次。 为什么？
因为禁运那几个月造成的伤害——通胀、企业成本爆炸、消费者荷包被掏空——已经像毒药一样渗进经济骨髓里了。
禁运结束不等于伤口自动愈合，市场只是晚了半拍才把真账算清楚。现在，历史在给我们发一模一样的剧本？越看越像？6月19号川普和伊朗要签订协议了？要达成和解，市场会狂欢呢？还是该哀悼呢？

2026年霍尔木兹海峡那边闹了好几个月，全球20%的石油运输通道实际卡住，中东多国产量大砍，供应冲击比1973年大多了。
2026年6月下旬因要达成和解的消息出来，油价回调到了70-80刀，这就跟1973年一样：禁运/冲突结束 ≠ 伤害消失。
所以会有以下3种情况发生：
1）停火谈成了，石油逐步恢复，但油价回不去60刀以下。通胀黏着，美联储不敢大放水。股会开始出现顶部进行回调10%，BTC也会伴随美股进行大力下跌到50000附近
2）如果重建超快 + 中国需求回暖 + 美联储真降息，油价砸下来，美股继续新高，BTC冲10万
3）黑天鹅：二次暴击，60天协商期停火谈崩，油价再次冲100-130刀。美股下跌20%，加密直接熊市模式，BTC回测5万以下。

我现在最倾向于 情景一：慢熊磨底 + 温和回调，而不是大崩盘或直接新高。概率我给60-65%左右。 为什么这么判断？
1. 川普宣布停火协议，霍尔木兹有望逐步重开（正式签字可能在6月19日左右），油价直接砸了4-5%，WTI掉到76-80刀区间，Brent也80出头。市场在狂欢“危机结束”。
但现实呢？海峡关闭好几个月，基础设施有损伤， tanker保险贵到离谱，船员不愿意跑，库存已经狂抽（IEA说3-4月就抽了2.5亿桶，OECD库存奔着历史低走，夏天需求高峰前可能见底）。重建+恢复正常流量，起码要3-6个月。
这就是1974年3月的翻版：headline利好，但底层成本（能源、物流、食品）已经涨上去，通胀黏在4.2%左右，美联储不敢大放水（利率3.5-3.75%死死按住，可能还hawkish）。企业盈利要下修，消费者荷包继续疼。
2.缓冲比1973大，但估值也更高，弹性就变脆好的一面：美国是页岩油大国，全球有更多替代供应，SPR虽然低但还在，AI和科技还在推增长。不会像70年代那样直接滞胀爆炸。
坏的一面：现在美股已经在高位（S&P 7500+附近，YTD还涨着）。一旦油价回不到60刀，通胀不快速下来，美联储不降反可能小幅加息，风险资产就容易被抽。
历史告诉我们：市场最危险的时候，就是所有人觉得“最坏已过”的时候。
3.其他情景为什么概率低乐观新高（情景二）：只有停火超级顺利 + 中国需求爆拉 + 油价快速砸回60刀以下，才可能。但目前库存太低、重建慢，短期可能再冲一下，但难持续。
（情景三）：停火谈崩或IRGC继续搞事，油价重回100-130+。黑天鹅概率15%左右，不是主流，但得防着（地缘永远是随机事件）。

总结我的观点： 这次最可能就是滞后算总账的过程。所以呢最简单的就是高空是一个不错的选择。具体会到什么位置呢？
我的预期：（不构成投资建议，后期会在币安策略群进行精细化调整）

translatedData.bodyTextOnly:
Today, I want to discuss a historical gem that many overlook—the oil embargo of 1973-1974. History doesn’t repeat itself exactly, but it often rhymes. What happened in 1973 bears a striking resemblance to what's unfolding in 2026.

Back in October 1973, the Arab nations imposed an embargo that choked global oil supply. Oil prices skyrocketed several times, and the US stock market took a hit of about 20%. The market was in a panic: "It's over, the energy crisis is deadly!"
In 2026, the war between Trump and Iran drove oil prices above $120, and the market started signaling an energy crisis is upon us.

It's thinking that since ETH is stronger than BTC, you can take the 'rotation' as a license to chase highs.

From noon to afternoon, BTC hovered around 65.6K while ETH held up relatively stronger. With the news of ETF fund differentiation, it's natural for many to conclude: BTC's weak, ETH's strong, let’s shift over.

This thought isn’t necessarily wrong.
But the danger lies in the fact that you might not be rotating; you could be chasing the sentiment that's already been pumped by others.

Today, Sam the French Fry is revisiting this mistake:
Just because the news tells you funds are differentiating doesn’t mean every split is a chase;
ETH being stronger than BTC doesn’t mean you can just jump in anywhere and find a good position;
If BTC continues to struggle below 66K, the market's risk appetite hasn't fully opened up yet.

My plan's boundaries are pretty straightforward:
If ETH is strong but BTC can’t reclaim 66K, I’ll treat it as short-term strength, not as confirmation of a major trend.
If ETH can hold after a pullback, it indicates that the funds aren’t just making a quick move.
If one candlestick completes without support, I’d rather miss out than force my way into the chaos.

Position discipline: In this kind of market, the biggest fear is 'understanding the direction but buying at the point others are cashing out.'

content:
【ETH跌64%反而让我更想买了，你们觉得现在该跑还是该抄？】

说真的，你们看到ETH现在价格的时候，什么感觉？

我猜大部分人心里想的是：完了，又跌了，赶紧跑。但我反而有点兴奋，不知道你们能不能理解这种心态。

我给你们打个比方。就像你看到菜市场打折，原来十块钱一斤的排骨降到三块钱一斤，虽然你不知道还会不会继续跌，但这个价格本身就很说明问题了——要么是这东西真的不值钱了，要么就是市场太恐慌了，便宜到离谱。

ETH现在的处境就是这样。从高点算下来跌了64%，那可是腰斩再腰斩。但奇怪的是什么呢？成交量最近异常放大，都超过市值的5%了，这种信号在大行情来临前经常能看到。

还有一件事我觉得挺有意思的。恐惧贪婪指数现在才22，属于极度恐惧区间，周均值更是低到17。翻译成人话就是：现在市场上的人怕得要死。但老韭菜都知道，极度恐惧往往是底部的标配啊。行情总是在绝望中诞生的嘛。

现在ETH在1725到1869这个区间震荡，涨了1%，一周下来涨了将近10%，在现在这种环境下其实不算差。说白了就是在选择方向，等成交量给信号。

我的判断是：如果能在1725上方稳住，这里可能就是底部区域；要是放量突破1869，那行情就来了。

当然，我只是说出我的观察，具体怎么做还得你自己决定。

你的信号方向是？

A. 多头信号，准备分批布局
B. 空头信号，等更低的位置
C. 观望，等方向明朗再说

🔥 FOMC Decision Day: What It Means for $BTC Right Now
The most important macro event of the month just landed — and Bitcoin is sitting at a critical crossroads.
Bitcoin is holding steady around $65,829 this morning, trading in a tight range as global investors pause aggressive positioning ahead of today’s Federal Reserve interest rate decision.
📰 What’s Happening
Today marks the FOMC rate decision — and it’s the first policy meeting led by new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, making his debut especially closely watched by markets worldwide. A rate hold is almost fully priced in, with CME data showing a 97.4% probability the Fed keeps rates in the 3.50%–3.75% range.
So the decision itself isn’t the real risk. The forward guidance and dot plot are.
📊 Why This Matters for Bitcoin
Two major tailwinds are already building behind Bitcoin right now:
1. Institutional demand returned — Spot Bitcoin ETFs broke a long outflow streak with $85.8 million in net inflows on June 13, the strongest single-day figure in about four weeks, led by BlackRock’s IBIT. Strategy added 1,587 BTC for $100 million between June 8–14, lifting its total holdings to 846,842 BTC. Whales also pulled over 11,000 BTC off exchanges — a classic accumulation signal pointing to reduced selling pressure.
2. Geopolitical relief — The U.S.–Iran deal moving toward resolution has eased oil prices and inflation fears, giving Bitcoin room to breathe.
🎯 Key Levels to Watch on $BTC
A dovish Fed tone or stable rate-path signal could push Bitcoin through $67,000 toward $68,500 and potentially $70,000.
On the downside, Bitcoin is expected to consolidate between $65,200 and $66,000 in the near term, with resistance near the $65,900–$66,000 zone.
Watch these levels:
🟢 Resistance: $67,000 → $68,500 → $70,000
🔴 Support: $65,200 → $63,000 → $60,000
💡 My Take
The market is coiled like a spring. Institutional money is quietly accumulating, whales are moving coins off exchanges, and ETF inflows are recovering. If Warsh signals even a slight dovish lean today, the pent-up demand could send Bitcoin sharply higher.
This is not the time to be on the sidelines.

BTC DeFi's TVL has evaporated by 60%, Rootstock admits: Retail investors are out, only the whales remain.

Is the BTC DeFi narrative over? Rootstock Labs execs dropped some truth bombs at BTC Prague: Total value locked (TVL) has plummeted from $180 billion last October to just $70 billion now, a drop of over 60%. Retail investors and hedge funds have basically exited, and projects are now pivoting to serve miners and digital asset treasury companies.

Translation: The C-end facing BTC DeFi narrative has cooled off. With TVL being slashed again and again, those projects that promised "passive income for every retail investor" have found that the real demand is only in the hands of a few whales holding large amounts of BTC. This isn’t decentralized finance; it's on-chain private banking.

Current BTC market watch: Price is $65,814, down 0.34% over 24h, funding rate at -0.005%, with shorts slightly favored but not extreme. The daily low of $65,329 has tested support, with volume at $7.6 billion, which isn’t exactly active, indicating a lack of market direction. $66,625 is the daily sell point, while a drop below $65,000 opens up downside potential.

Rootstock's transition is quite honest—rather than chasing generic DeFi customer acquisition, they’re focusing on real asset liability needs to build products. Miners need liquidity without selling their BTC, which is a must-have. But the DeFi story has shifted from "financial democratization for all" to "providing lending services to whales," which is a bit ironic.

Liquidity doesn’t lie: When money leaves, it’s gone, and no matter how big the pie you paint, it won’t keep them around.

title: Binance Wallet Launches Web3 API, Expanding Access to On-Chain Trading Infrastructure
subTitle:
June 17, 2026
Binance has announced the launch of its new Web3 API, a move aimed at giving developers, institutions, and advanced traders direct programmable access to on-chain trading and market data through Binance Wallet infrastructure.
The new product marks another step in Binance’s broader push beyond traditional exchange services, as the company continues expanding deeper into Web3 tools and blockchain-based financial infrastructure.
According to Binance, the Web3 API is designed to help users build applications that can access real-time market data, swap quotes, and on-chain transaction execution through a single integration. The company says this could simplify development for teams building trading bots, portfolio management tools, decentralized applications, and other Web3 services.
A Push Toward Simpler Web3 Development.
One of the biggest challenges in Web3 development has been fragmentation. Developers often need to connect to multiple services for pricing data, liquidity access, wallet functionality, and transaction routing. Binance says its new API aims to reduce that complexity by offering a more unified solution.
The company stated that the Web3 API allows users to integrate on-chain trading, wallet capabilities, and market data directly into their applications without managing several separate integrations. This could make it easier for both startups and larger institutions to launch blockchain-based products faster.
Binance also emphasized that the API is built for flexibility, scalability, and security, suggesting that it is targeting not only retail-focused builders but also enterprise users looking for more reliable infrastructure.
Key Features of the New Binance Web3 API.
Binance highlighted several features in the launch announcement that may appeal to developers and professional market participants.
The API includes access to real-time token prices, candlestick data, and information on top gainers and losers across supported chains. It also offers trading functionality, including aggregated swap quotes from multiple vendors and the ability to facilitate on-chain transactions.
Another major feature is multi-chain support. Binance says the Web3 API can be used across several EVM-compatible networks, including Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Arbitrum, Polygon, Base, Optimism, and Linea, while also supporting Solana. The company added that more chains are expected in the future.
Binance further noted that the API includes built-in MEV protection mechanisms, although it also clarified that such protection cannot be guaranteed under all market conditions.
Non-Custodial Structure May Appeal to Web3 Users.
A notable part of the announcement is Binance’s emphasis on the API’s non-custodial design. According to the company, Binance Wallet does not hold or access user private keys. Instead, the API returns unsigned transactions, which users must sign locally in their own wallets.
That structure may be important for developers and institutions that want access to Binance’s infrastructure while still maintaining user-side control over wallet security and transaction authorization.
Binance also said the service is backed by its wallet infrastructure and includes 24/7 technical support, positioning the offering as enterprise-ready.
Who Binance Is Targeting?
The launch appears to be aimed at a broad but highly specific audience. Binance says the Web3 API is designed for developers building decentralized applications, trading bots, and on-chain tools. It is also intended for institutions that want to integrate blockchain trading features into existing systems, as well as advanced traders looking for programmable access to swaps across multiple networks.
The company also mentioned AI agent builders who want to add wallet-based on-chain actions into automated workflows. This is particularly interesting because AI-powered crypto tools have become one of the most discussed trends in the digital asset industry throughout 2026.
Why This Matters for Binance.
The launch of the Web3 API shows that Binance is continuing to position itself as more than just a crypto exchange. In recent years, competition in the digital asset industry has increasingly shifted toward infrastructure, developer tools, and ecosystem services.
By offering a unified API for on-chain trading and wallet functionality, Binance may be aiming to strengthen its role in the next phase of crypto adoption, where developers and institutions need scalable tools to build products rather than simply access markets.
The move could also help Binance capture demand from businesses that want exposure to Web3 functionality without building every component themselves.
Important Limitations and Risk Notes:
Binance noted that the Web3 API is only available in regions where Binance Wallet is supported. The company also reminded users that product availability may vary depending on local regulations and jurisdictions.
In its disclaimer, Binance said the Web3 API is provided as a technology service and does not constitute investment, brokerage, custody, or regulated financial services. The company also warned users about the risks associated with digital asset trading, including volatility, slippage, smart contract vulnerabilities, and the possibility of losing funds.
Final Takeaway:
Binance’s new Web3 API launch reflects a growing trend across the crypto industry. Platforms are increasingly competing not only for traders but also for developers, institutions, and infrastructure market share.
If adoption continues to grow, the API could become an important bridge between centralized platform infrastructure and decentralized on-chain execution. For Binance, that could mean a stronger position in the evolving Web3 economy. For developers and institutions, it may provide a faster and more efficient way to build blockchain-based products at scale.

title: Ринок на роздоріжжі: чому BTC тримається, а ETH "штормить"? 📉🌪️
subTitle:
Червень 2026 року виявився для криптоінвесторів справжнім випробуванням на витривалість. Якщо ви стежите за графіками, то бачите різницю: $BTC  виглядає як "тиха гавань" порівняно з альткоїнами.

Що відбувається прямо зараз?

BTC vs Macro: Після того, як дані по CPI (інфляції) в США вийшли в межах очікувань, ринок видихнув. Біткоїн стабілізувався в діапазоні $62k-$64k. Велика увага зараз прикута до засідання ФРС (16-17 червня) — це ключовий момент, який визначить тренд на найближчі місяці.

Ethereum: Тут ситуація складніша. $ETH  цьогоріч показує слабкість порівняно з біткоїном, а співвідношення ETH/BTC впало до 10-місячних мінімумів. Перенесення оновлення "Glamsterdam" на 3-й квартал і відтоки з ETF додали тиску на ціну.

Інституції: Цікаво спостерігати за стратегією великих гравців — ми бачимо, як "кити" (як-от MicroStrategy) продовжують накопичувати BTC навіть під час волатильності, що слугує певним сигналом для ринку.

Моя думка:

Зараз не час для панічних продажів. Ринки на дні часто виглядають нудними або страшними, але саме тут "розумні гроші" накопичують активи.

translatedData.content: Having multiple models isn't just about having a longer menu; the key is whether the tasks are placed correctly. Today, I want to chat about another issue in OpenGradient Chat: how to actually use multiple models. Many AI products flood the menu with model names, thinking that more choices equal a stronger product. But the real issue for everyday users isn't 'how many models exist in the world,' but rather 'which one should I hand this task to?' Writing a public piece, organizing a trade recap, generating an event graphic, discussing a sensitive personal issue—each of these tasks has different requirements for speed, style, privacy, and boundaries. #ETH  So, I care more about whether OpenGradient Chat can create a clear execution path for model selection instead of just a flashy list. For example, general queries can prioritize speed, creative tasks can focus on style, and sensitive content should go into Private Chat, which emphasizes privacy boundaries. Users want clarity, not just a bunch of buttons, but an understanding of why this path suits the current task. #BTC  This is where OpenGradient can differentiate itself from regular AI tools. Behind it, there's talk of verifiable, confidential computing, TEE, and proof of inference, but when it reaches the user, it shouldn't turn into a jargon fest. The truly useful expression should be: I present a task in chat.opengradient.ai, and the system helps me clearly understand which model, mode, privacy level to choose, and whether the results can be reviewed. From the perspective of creators in the plaza, this scenario is also quite straightforward. We write content daily, and it’s not just about getting an 'answer'; it's about judging: is this suitable for public discussion? Will this prompt expose unreleased ideas? Is this model appropriate for inference, rewriting, or visual creativity? If all these choices could remain within the same OpenGradient Chat workspace, user stickiness would gradually build up. The position of $OPG  can also be understood here. It shouldn't just be an activity tag; instead, we should observe if it can connect with credits, model calls, Private Chat, and ongoing usage actions. Only when product actions are consistently happening will the token narrative not drift in the air. @OpenGradient  $OPG  #OPG

content:
多模型不是菜单越长越好，关键是任务能不能放对位置
今天看我想聊 OpenGradient Chat 里的另一个问题：多模型到底应该怎么用。
很多 AI 产品一上来就把模型名字铺满菜单，好像选择越多，产品越强。但普通用户真正遇到的麻烦不是“不知道世界上有几个模型”，而是不知道自己这个任务该交给谁。写一段公开文案、整理一份交易复盘、生成一张活动配图、讨论一个不想外泄的私人问题，这些任务对速度、风格、隐私、边界的要求都不一样。#ETH 
所以我更在意 OpenGradient Chat 能不能把多模型选择做成一套清楚的执行路径，而不是一个炫技列表。比如普通问题可以追求速度，创意任务可以看风格，敏感内容则应该放进 Private Chat 这种更强调私密边界的入口。用户要的不是一堆按钮，而是知道这条路为什么适合当前任务。#BTC 
这也是 OpenGradient 和普通 AI 工具可以拉开差距的地方。它背后讲的是可验证、保密计算、TEE、推理证明这些基础设施，但落到用户手里，最好不要变成一堆术语。真正有用的表达应该是：我在 chat.opengradient.ai 里提出一个任务，系统能让我更清楚地知道该选什么模型、什么模式、什么隐私等级，以及结果是否能被复盘。
从广场创作者角度看，这个场景也很直接。我们每天写内容，不只是要一个“回答”，而是要判断：这段适合公开讨论吗？这个提示词会不会暴露未发布思路？这个模型适不适合做推理、改写或视觉创意？如果这些选择都能留在同一个 OpenGradient Chat 工作台里，使用黏性才会慢慢出来。
$OPG 的位置也可以放在这里理解。它不该只是活动标签，而应该观察它以后能不能和 credits、模型调用、Private Chat、持续使用这些动作连接起来。只有产品动作持续发生，代币叙事才不会飘在空中。

translatedData.content: OpenGradient Chat's multi-model entry isn't just about an extended drink menu. Today’s question is: with more and more AI models, do users need a longer drink menu or a quieter ordering spot? Right now, it's all too easy for AI products to flaunt their 'model count' as a selling point: there's one that excels at writing, another that’s great at reasoning, and one that’s a better conversationalist, more suited for open discussions and brainstorming. #ETH  Having multiple models is definitely useful. But if every time a user switches models, it's like changing tables: one spot for work solutions, another for personal judgment, one for creative trials, and a different one for retrospectives, then the problem goes beyond mere inconvenience. The issue is that context and privacy get fragmented. What you really want might not be a wall full of bottles but rather a table where you can switch cups based on the scenario: need rigor? Switch to a model better suited for reasoning; want divergence? Go for a more open model; want to explore visuals? Step into Image Studio; but the whole process still happens in the same more private entryway. #BTC  So when I look at OpenGradient Chat’s multi-model setup, I won’t just be checking how fresh the names are. The official recommended materials mention that OpenGradient Chat integrates Claude Fable 5, and there are options like Nous Hermes in Private Chat. If this point was merely summarized as 'more models', it would sound pretty ordinary. What’s truly worth noting is: once these models are integrated into OpenGradient Chat, can users switch tools based on questions in a private-by-default environment, rather than having to move based on tools? This is crucial for AI Chat. Because users don’t all ask the same kind of questions. Some require a calm breakdown of logic, some need a sentence to sound more human, others want to boldly explore directions, and some just want to unload the chaotic thoughts in their heads. Different models are like different drink glasses; it’s not about being the most expensive, but about matching the glass to the drink’s context. @OpenGradient  $OPG  #OPG

问题是上下文和隐私会被拆散。

有的问题需要冷静拆逻辑，有的问题需要把一句话写得更像人，有的问题需要大胆试方向，有的问题只是想把脑子里乱糟糟的东西倒出来。不同模型像不同酒杯，不是越贵越好，而是要和这杯酒的场景匹配。

用户是来试一次，还是会回来继续用？

title: Why Fear Creates More Millionaires Than Bull Markets
subTitle:
Every investor says they want to buy low and sell high.
Yet when prices fall, most people do the exact opposite.
They panic.
They wait.
They hesitate.
And often, they miss the opportunity they were waiting for.
The Psychology of Market Fear
Fear is one of the strongest forces in financial markets.
When prices drop, negative headlines spread quickly.
Social media becomes filled with pessimism.
Many investors start questioning their long-term strategy.
But experienced investors understand something important:
Fear creates discounts.
And discounts create opportunities.
Bitcoin's Historical Pattern
$BTC has experienced multiple corrections throughout its history.
Every major bull cycle included periods where investors believed the market was finished.
Yet Bitcoin continued to recover, innovate, and attract new participants.
This doesn't guarantee future performance.
However, it reminds us that market sentiment can change much faster than people expect.
Ethereum and Innovation
While short-term traders focus on price movements, many long-term investors continue watching $ETH because of its role in blockchain infrastructure.
Innovation doesn't stop simply because the market becomes volatile.
Development continues.
Adoption continues.
New applications continue to emerge.
That is why many investors focus on long-term trends rather than daily price swings.
Why BNB Remains on Watchlists

This morning, I finally resolved a rookie mistake where I misconfigured my private key as an environment variable, almost causing my testnet Gas to get drained. Rubbing my temples, I opened up OpenGradient, which has been buzzing in the crypto circle these past few days. They just launched an 'OpenGradient Chat', claiming to be a privacy-first decentralized model assistant. As an old-timer constantly bombarded with 'AI+Web3' pitch decks, my first thought was: Whoa, is this just another fundraising scam?

But I had no choice; the discussions in the @OpenGradient  community were too heated, with links being shared daily. So, I took the time to dive into their (Bedrock ❌ should be called OpenGradient) whitepaper, even lurking in their Discord community and checking the on-chain explorer. Wow, I didn't realize until I looked—OpenGradient actually has some decent tech architecture backing it up.
#OPG 
Following their official whitepaper and developer documentation, I set up my local Python 3.13 environment and got the SDK sorted with pip install opengradient, ready to experience their core x402 LLM inference. I was shocked to find that, according to the on-chain explorer, there are only 3 active nodes! Checking out those full nodes and contract interaction records, the total transaction volume is just over 800,000. You paint such a grand vision in your marketing, but the actual number of hardware nodes on-chain is pitifully low. #BTC 

However, the newly launched OpenGradient Chat does hit the mark on privacy. The whitepaper states that it completely separates users' IPs and sent content through opaque HTTP relays, then decrypts and runs them inside a hardware-backed TEE. I tried it on the web interface, and it's aggregated several mainstream models like ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok, even allowing side-by-side output comparisons. #ETH 

In terms of user experience, the response speed is indeed very fast; you barely feel like it's routing through a 'decentralized' pathway, and you don't need to register any real-name info, which is a big improvement over the Web2 models that frequently ban accounts. $OPG 

After reading the whitepaper, I feel like OpenGradient aims to be the 'AI co-processor' for Web3. At this stage, it's worth checking out their privacy Chat for fun, but if you’re considering betting real money on its future, you really need to stay vigilant.

Details 
Traders now turn to Warsh's debut press conference for clues how the central bank's communication will change under his leadership.
The Federal Reserve left its benchmark fed funds rate range unchanged at 3.50%-3.75% on Wednesday, a move markets had expected nearly unanimously.

This was the first U.S. central bank policy meeting led by Kevin Warsh, who took over as chair from Jerome Powell after being confirmed by the Senate last month.

The focus now shifts to Warsh's post-meeting press conference, beginning at 2:30 p.m. ET, and to what he says about the road ahead under his leadership at the central bank.
Markets have spent the past several months steadily dialing back expectations for any rate cuts as inflation proved more stubborn and labor market data remained resilient. Traders now see a growing chance that the Fed's next move could be a rate hike rather than a cut.

Warsh's comments could carry added weight because he has previously criticized the Fed's use of forward guidance and quarterly economic projections, including the closely watched dot plot.

Investors will be looking for signs of whether the central bank plans to communicate policy differently under his leadership.

Stablecoins have the potential to significantly transform global payments by combining the speed of cryptocurrencies with the price stability of traditional currencies.
Why Stablecoins Are Attractive for Payments
Faster Cross-Border Transfers Traditional international payments can take several days to settle. Stablecoins can enable transfers within minutes, regardless of the sender's or receiver's location.Lower Transaction Costs Cross-border payments often involve multiple banks and intermediaries. Stablecoins can reduce these costs by allowing value to move directly on blockchain networks.24/7 Availability Unlike traditional banking systems, blockchain networks operate around the clock, allowing payments to be sent and received at any time.Greater Financial Inclusion People without access to traditional banking services can potentially participate in the global economy using only a smartphone and an internet connection.
Challenges to Adoption Regulatory uncertainty in many countries. Compliance requirements such as anti-money laundering (AML) and know-your-customer (KYC) rules. Dependence on stablecoin issuers to maintain reserves and transparency. Integration with existing financial infrastructure. Leading Stablecoins
Some of the most widely used stablecoins include:
Tether (USDT) USD Coin (USDC) DAI (DAI) Potential Impact
If adoption continues to grow, stablecoins could streamline remittances, international trade settlements, payroll payments, and online commerce. Businesses may benefit from faster settlement times, while consumers could enjoy cheaper and more accessible financial services.
Conclusion
Stablecoins are emerging as one of the most practical uses of blockchain technology. While regulatory and operational challenges remain, their ability to facilitate fast, low-cost, and global transactions positions them as a potentially transformative force in the future of payments.

【ETH 这根阳线，是反弹还是陷阱？】

昨晚 ETH 悄悄拉到 1788，快到 1800 了。有人喊牛市来了，有人说是死猫跳。

我上周说过，1725 是生命线，跌破就清仓。结果呢？没破，撑住了，还在上面走了将近 10%。

说实话，我也没想到这么硬。

FGI 22，极度恐慌。历史数据告诉我们，这种时候往往不是顶部，是底部。BTC 占比 56.4%，资金在抱团主流币，ETH 被压着但没崩，这就是信号。

现在最关键的问题：成交量有没有跟上。

DeFi lock-up plummets 60%, but Bitcoin DeFi is eyeing miner wallets

📍 Event Background

The DeFi market is undergoing a silent "de-dumbing down". Richard Green, head of the Rootstock Labs institution and ecosystem, revealed at the BTC Prague 2026 conference that as the Total Value Locked (TVL) in DeFi protocols dropped from around $180 billion last October to about $70 billion now—over a 60% decline—Bitcoin DeFi projects are strategically shifting focus—from servicing a broad base of crypto-native traders to targeting a more affluent niche group.

📋 Key Content Breakdown

1. Massive DeFi liquidity withdrawal: TVL down from $180 billion to $70 billion, with many crypto-native traders and hedge funds exiting the scene
2. Rootstock's strategic pivot: target users shifting from "general DeFi users" to Bitcoin miners and digital asset treasury companies
3. New product positioning: offering lending and yield products for BTC whales, catering to the need for liquidity without selling assets
4. Nature of demand: Bitcoin DeFi demand is not widespread but concentrated among "a few financially strong niche groups"
5. Key Insight: The core focus for projects is no longer on scaling customer acquisition but on designing products around real asset-liability needs

🔑 Core Logic Analysis

This round of DeFi liquidity shrinkage is not a short-term fluctuation but a structural shift. When TVL evaporated by over $110 billion, previously active DeFi players—crypto hedge funds, quant trading teams, retail LPs—mostly exited or significantly reduced their exposure. The traditional DeFi's "casting a wide net" model has failed.

However, Green pointed out an overlooked truth: Bitcoin holders, especially miners and treasury companies, hold a large amount of "dormant" BTC assets. These entities have real asset-liability needs—requiring liquidity to cover operational costs (miners) or seeking returns without selling core holdings (treasury companies). Rootstock's transformation is essentially about finding a "high-net-worth niche market" amid the DeFi winter.

Delving deeper, this reflects the uniqueness of the Bitcoin ecosystem. Unlike Ethereum DeFi, Bitcoin DeFi naturally targets "long-term holders" and "institutional players" because BTC's volatility and holding cost structure dictate that only players with sufficiently large capital have the incentive to engage BTC in DeFi protocols instead of simply holding.

💡 Impact on the Crypto Market

1. Bitcoin DeFi may carve out a different development path from Ethereum DeFi—more institutionalized, more vertical, and more reliant on real use cases rather than speculative incentives
2. Miners and treasury companies becoming the new DeFi demand engine, potentially providing structural support for Bitcoin sidechain tokens like RBTC
3. If more projects follow Rootstock's pivot, the DeFi industry could shift from a "retail casino" to an "institutional toolbox"

- DeFi TVL: $180 billion to $70 billion (-61%)
- Rootstock: the first and longest-running Bitcoin sidechain, EVM compatible
- Security: over 80% of Bitcoin hash rate protection through merged mining
- BTC Prague 2026: June 11-13, featuring a specialized breakfast meeting for miners/institutions hosted by Rootstock and Xapo Bank

DeFi市场正在经历一场静默的"去散户化"。Rootstock Labs机构与生态负责人Richard Green在BTC Prague 2026会议上透露，随着DeFi协议总锁仓价值（TVL）从去年10月的约1800亿美元骤降至当前约700亿美元，跌幅超过60%，比特币DeFi项目正在战略转型——从服务广泛的加密原生交易者，转向深耕资金实力更强的细分群体。

这轮DeFi流动性萎缩并非短期波动，而是结构性转变。当TVL蒸发超过1100亿美元时，曾经活跃的DeFi玩家——加密对冲基金、量化交易团队、散户LP——大多已退出或大幅收缩敞口。传统DeFi的"广撒网"模式失效了。

但Green指出了一个被忽视的真相：比特币持有者，特别是矿工和财库公司，持有大量"沉睡"的BTC资产。这些实体有真实的资产负债表需求——需要流动性来支付运营成本（矿工）、或希望在不出售核心持仓的情况下获取收益（财库公司）。Rootstock的转型本质上是在DeFi寒冬中寻找"高净值 niche 市场"。

更深一层看，这反映了比特币生态的独特性。与以太坊DeFi不同，比特币DeFi天然面向"长期持有者"和"机构级玩家"，因为BTC的波动性和持有成本结构决定了：只有资金体量足够大的玩家，才有动力将BTC投入DeFi协议而非简单持有。

我这次更想从 Agent 角度理解 OpenGradient。未来 Web3 里的 AI，不会只停留在回答问题，它会帮用户读数据、筛策略、生成交易建议、执行自动化任务，甚至接入多个应用形成连续决策。如果这个过程中，模型调用、外部数据、推理结果、支付结算全部依赖中心化黑箱，那 Agent 再强，也只是一个包装精致的接口。

What is Hyperliquid? A DEX with its own blockchain

- Hyperliquid is a decentralized exchange (DEX) specializing in perpetual futures, built on its own high-performance Layer 1 blockchain.
- Not operating on existing platforms like Ethereum, Hyperliquid utilizes a custom blockchain optimized for high-frequency trading, delivering speed and low costs.
- The exchange uses a fully on-chain order book instead of an AMM (automated market maker) model, allowing direct order matching between buyers and sellers, reducing slippage.
- Thanks to the HyperBFT consensus mechanism, transactions are confirmed in milliseconds, processing up to 100,000 orders per second with no gas fees for transactions.
- HYPE is the native token of the ecosystem, used for staking, governance participation, and paying gas fees on HyperEVM.

Just finished tweaking a bunch of spreadsheets, and on a whim, I tried out a few AI tools. The most striking takeaway is: everyone’s chasing more powerful models, but not many are asking—who's actually computing these answers? Is the input being taken away? Can the results be verified? That’s also why I revisited @OpenGradient .
I found that OpenGradient isn’t just about "hooking AI onto the chain"; it’s about breaking down AI reasoning into a verifiable execution process. In traditional AI services, users send prompts to a platform, and basically, you can only trust the platform with where the model runs, whether it’s tampered with, and how the input is handled. OpenGradient's approach is more foundational: it allows models to run on a dedicated decentralized node network and, through TEE, proof generation, on-chain settlement, and other mechanisms, strives to make the "model, input, output, and execution environment" as traceable and auditable as possible.
Here, OpenGradient Chat is crucial. It’s not just a simple chat shell; it places the most accessible entry point for regular users on top of privacy and trusted execution. When users ask questions through Chat, the front-end experience feels like a normal AI assistant, but behind the scenes, it emphasizes local encryption, anonymized routing, and secure execution environments, aiming to ensure that prompts aren’t easily tied to a user's identity. This is important for AI applications because many future questions will involve trading judgments, health consultations, legal dilemmas, and personal planning. If the entry point itself lacks privacy design, no matter how strong the model is, people will hesitate to ask.
The value of $OPG  also needs to be understood within this computational network. It’s not just about slapping an AI label on it; it revolves around inference calls, node incentives, verification settlements, and the formation of a model ecosystem. Developers can utilize the SDK to call ML/LLM reasoning, manage models, and deploy automated workflows; on the user side, they experience a more accessible private AI interaction through OpenGradient Chat.
I believe OpenGradient genuinely wants to tackle the trust layer issue in the AI era: answers can be smart, but what's more important is that the underlying computation process can be verified. For AI to enter finance, on-chain agency, automated strategies, and personal privacy scenarios, having model capability isn't enough; we also need trusted execution, privacy isolation, and auditable infrastructure. #OPG  #BTC #ETH

This morning while scanning the charts, I initially just wanted to look at a few short-term rotations in the AI sector, but I found many projects still talking about 'model shelling'. What really made me stop and dive deeper was @OpenGradient , because it’s not just about creating a simple AI application; it aims to reorganize AI models, inference calls, and on-chain settlement.
I understand that the core of OpenGradient isn't just 'putting AI on-chain', but transforming AI models into network resources that can be invoked, priced, verified, and distributed. In traditional AI platforms, models are usually controlled by centralized companies, where developers have to access APIs, pay with credit cards, and cater to the platform's whims; whereas OpenGradient is more like placing models into an open market: model providers can publish models, callers can use them as needed, and the fees are settled through $OPG , turning the whole process from a 'black box service' into a 'composable on-chain infrastructure'.
This is also crucial for OpenGradient Chat. On the surface, Chat appears to be a dialogue between users and models, but behind the scenes, it’s actually a multi-model invocation gateway: users are not just asking questions; they are invoking smart capabilities from the network. If in the future every conversation, every agent inference, and every data analysis can correspond to a clear model source, invocation cost, and settlement path, then AI will no longer just be a web product, but will transform into executable modules that can be directly embedded in Web3 applications.

Fidelity joins Wall Street's race to manage stablecoin reserves.

Fidelity Investments is the latest Wall Street firm seeking a role in one of the fastest-growing corners of digital assets: managing the reserves that back stablecoins.

The asset manager is launching the Fidelity Reserves Digital Fund, a money market fund designed for stablecoin issuers and institutional investors under the reserve requirements established by the recently enacted $GENIUS Act, on Thursday.

The launch comes just days after State Street unveiled a similar product, the State Street Stablecoin Reserves Money Market Fund, underscoring how traditional financial firms are increasingly competing for a market that could swell into the trillions of dollars if stablecoins become a larger part of the global financial system.

Stablecoins — digital tokens pegged to assets such as the U.S. dollar — have grown into a roughly $320 billion market and are widely used for trading, payments and cross-border transfers. Industry forecasts cited by State Street project the sector could expand to between $1.9 trillion and $4 trillion by 2030 as institutional adoption increases.

That growth would create a corresponding pool of reserve assets that must be invested in highly liquid instruments.

The $GENIUS Act, signed into law last year, established the first federal framework for payment stablecoins in the United States. Among other requirements, issuers must hold reserves in cash, short-term Treasury securities and certain government money market funds.

The legislation has created an opportunity for traditional asset managers to offer regulated vehicles that stablecoin issuers can use to manage those reserves while generating yield.

Fidelity's fund will invest in U.S. Treasury bills, notes and bonds with maturities of 93 days or less, cash, overnight repurchase agreements backed by Treasuries and other government money market funds that comply with the law.
